label: History
value: Dorothy lived on a farm in Kansas
unit: Dorothy grew up as an orphan in Kansas on a farm with her Uncle Henry and Aunt Em. A sudden cyclone carried her house into the Land of Oz, landing on and killing the Wicked Witch of the East. To find a way back home, she set out for the Emerald City alongside her dog Toto, meeting the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion along the way. Sent by Oz to eliminate the Wicked Witch of the West, Dorothy accidentally destroyed the Witch by throwing a bucket of water over her. After further travels, Glinda the Good revealed that her magic Silver Shoes could carry her home, and she clapped her heels together to return to Kansas. Later, Dorothy accompanied Uncle Henry on a sea voyage, but was swept overboard in a violent storm while clinging to a chicken-coop along with a yellow hen named Billina. They landed in the Land of Ev, where Dorothy discovered and wound up the mechanical man Tiktok and was captured by Princess Langwidere. Rescued by Princess Ozma and her old friends from Oz, Dorothy assisted in defeating the Nome King and rescuing the royal family of Ev. Following a joyful visit to the Emerald City, Dorothy used the Nome King's magic belt to join her ailing uncle in Australia, arranging for Ozma to check on her weekly through a magic picture.

passages.v01:c03:p0000: Dorothy lived in the midst of the great Kansas prairies, with Uncle Henry, who was a farmer, and Aunt Em, who was the farmer’s wife. Their house was small, for the lumber to build it had to be carried by wagon many miles. There were four walls, a floor and a roof, which made one room; and this room contained a rusty looking cookstove, a cupboard for the dishes, a table, three or four chairs, and the beds. Uncle Henry and Aunt Em had a big bed in one corner, and Dorothy a little bed in another corner. There was no garret at all, and no cellar—except a small hole dug in the ground, called a cyclone cellar, where the family could go in case one of those great whirlwinds arose, mighty enough to crush any building in its path. It was reached by a trap door in the middle of the floor, from which a ladder led down into the small, dark hole.

Upon reaching the Emerald City, the Wizard required them to defeat the Wicked Witch of the West before granting his wish. During the battle against the Witch's minions, the Scarecrow single-handedly killed forty wild crows. After the Witch's defeat, the Wizard satisfied the Scarecrow's desire by filling his head with bran, needles, and pins. When the Wizard departed in his balloon, the Scarecrow was made the ruler of the Emerald City. He was later deposed by General Jinjur's Army of Revolt and escaped alongside Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse to seek aid from the Tin Woodman and Glinda. After losing his original straw filling to Jackdaws, his clothes were stuffed with banknotes, making him immensely valuable. Glinda subsequently established that Princess Ozma was the rightful ruler of Oz, whereupon the Tin Woodman appointed the Scarecrow as Royal Treasurer. Later, he joined Ozma's expedition to the Nome Kingdom to rescue the royal family of Ev, where he was temporarily transformed into a gold ornament by the Nome King before being restored.

label: History

unit: Dorothy grew up as an orphan in Kansas on a farm with her Uncle Henry and Aunt Em. A sudden cyclone carried her house into the Land of Oz, landing on and killing the Wicked Witch of the East. To find a way back home, she set out for the Emerald City alongside her dog Toto, meeting the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion along the way. Sent by Oz to eliminate the Wicked Witch of the West, Dorothy accidentally destroyed the Witch by throwing a bucket of water over her. After further travels, Glinda the Good revealed that her magic Silver Shoes could carry her home, and she clapped her heels together to return to Kansas. Later, Dorothy accompanied Uncle Henry on a sea voyage, but was swept overboard in a violent storm while clinging to a chicken-coop along with a yellow hen named Billina. They landed in the Land of Ev, where Dorothy discovered and wound up the mechanical man Tiktok and was captured by Princess Langwidere. Rescued by Princess Ozma and her old friends from Oz, Dorothy assisted in defeating the Nome King and rescuing the royal family of Ev. Following a joyful visit to the Emerald City, Dorothy used the Nome King's magic belt to join her ailing uncle in Australia, arranging for Ozma to check on her weekly through a magic picture.

label: History
value: The Witch has a powerful single eye
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West conquered the West country of the Land of Oz and made the Winkies her slaves by using the magical Golden Cap to command the Winged Monkeys. She also used the cap's charm a second time to defeat the Great Oz and drive him out of the West. When Dorothy and her companions traveled into her territory under orders from Oz to destroy her, the Witch spotted them from her castle with her powerful single eye. She sent her pack of wolves, flock of wild crows, swarm of black bees, and a group of Winkie slaves to kill or scare them, but all were defeated in turn. Forced to use the Golden Cap's third and final charm, she commanded the Winged Monkeys to destroy the Tin Woodman and Scarecrow, capture the Lion, and carry Dorothy safely to her castle. Because Dorothy bore the kiss of the Good Witch of the North and wore the Silver Shoes, the Witch dared not harm her directly and instead forced her to work as a kitchen slave while attempting to starve the Lion into submission. Desiring the immense power of the Silver Shoes, the Witch tricked Dorothy by making an invisible iron bar on the kitchen floor to trip her, causing one shoe to fall off so she could snatch it. In anger, Dorothy threw a bucket of water over the Witch, unaware that water would dissolve her. The Witch wailed in despair as she melted into a shapeless brown mass on the floor, leaving only the single silver shoe behind.
